# Purpose and scope

This Process Transfer Plan (**PTP-001**) defines the strategy and scope for transferring the
A-Mab drug-substance (DS) manufacturing process from the **sending site**
(`{python} SENDING_SITE`) to the **receiving site** (`{python} RECEIVING_SITE`). It
transfers the process knowledge developed and characterized during Stage 1 (Process Design)
— the parameter classifications, proven acceptable ranges, multivariate design spaces and
per-CQA control strategy captured in the process-characterization package — to the
commercial DS facility, and defines the site-equivalency analysis, the scale-down-model and
comparability strategy, the transfer of the manufacturing process, analytical methods and
control strategy, the PPQ / batch strategy, and the gap analysis that governs execution.

**Scope.** The `{python} n_steps`-step commercial-scale A-Mab DS process (production
bioreactor through final UF/DF) at the `{python} f"{scale_l:,}"`-L commercial scale,
including the transfer of the validated analytical methods and the control strategy. Drug-
product (fill/finish) transfer and the formulation characterization are addressed under the
drug-product program and are out of scope. This plan governs the transfer strategy; the
receiving-site validation (PPQ) is executed under the site validation plan and confirmed in
the Process Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**).

**Basis.** The transfer follows the technology-transfer good practices of ICH Q10 [@ichq10] and the lifecycle transfer strategy of the FDA 2011 process-validation guidance [@fda2011], within the QbD framework of ICH Q8, Q9, Q10 and Q11
[@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq10; @ichq11] and the process model and control-strategy framework of
the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. The process knowledge transferred is that established in the
per-unit-operation characterization plans and reports and consolidated in the Process
Characterization Master Plan (**PCMP-001**) and Master Report (**PCMR-001**).

# Transfer strategy

The transfer applies the enhanced (QbD) approach: because the process was developed and
characterized against a defined set of CQAs with multivariate design spaces and a per-CQA
control strategy, the transfer is a **knowledge transfer** of that understanding to the
receiving site, confirmed by site-equivalency analysis, engineering runs and a commercial-scale
PPQ campaign rather than by re-development. The strategy comprises, consistent with the FDA process-validation lifecycle
[@fda2011]: (i) a product and process description carried from the characterization package;
(ii) a site-equivalency analysis comparing the sending and receiving equipment, facilities and
utilities; (iii) a scale-down-model and comparability strategy that bridges development and
commercial scale; (iv) transfer of the manufacturing process, the analytical methods and the
control strategy; (v) a PPQ / batch strategy that confirms the CPPs, the design spaces and the
cumulative viral clearance at commercial scale; and (vi) a gap analysis with mitigations. The
criticality analysis and risk assessments are confirmed at the receiving site (**RA-001**,
**PCMP-001**).

# Product and process description

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody produced by fed-batch cell culture and purified
by a platform train. The commercial process operates at `{python} f"{scale_l:,}"` L with a
nominal titre of `{python} f"{titer:g}"` g/L and an overall DS yield of
`{python} pct(overall_yield)`, delivering approximately `{python} f"{ds_mass_kg:.1f}"` kg of
drug substance at `{python} f"{ds_conc:g}"` g/L. The `{python} n_steps` unit operations, and
each step's principal role in the control strategy, are summarized in @tbl-steps.


: The A-Mab drug-substance process train (Steps 3–10) and each step's principal role in the control strategy. {#tbl-steps}

The process controls `{python} n_cqa` drug-substance CQAs. Their acceptance criteria and
criticality, established in the characterization package, are the quality targets the transfer
must preserve; the integrated control strategy delivers them with a minimum commercial-scale
capability of **Cpk = `{python} f"{min_cpk:.2f}"`** and cumulative viral clearance of
`{python} f"{lrv_x:.2f}"` log₁₀ (XMuLV) and `{python} f"{lrv_m:.2f}"` log₁₀ (MVM).

# Site-equivalency analysis

A site-equivalency analysis compares the receiving-site equipment train, facilities and
utilities against the sending-site (and scale-down) reference to assure they are equivalent and
qualified for commercial manufacture [@fda2011; @ichq10]. The analysis covers, for each unit
operation: the equipment make, operating principle and qualification status; the operating
ranges for the CPPs and WC-CPPs at the new scale; the buffer, media and consumable supply; the
automation and control system; and the personnel qualification and training. Any
non-equivalence is captured as a transfer gap (§11) with a mitigation and is resolved before the
PPQ campaign. Equivalency is confirmed by engineering runs at commercial scale prior to PPQ.

# Scale-down model and comparability strategy

The commercial-scale process is bridged to the characterization data by the **qualified
scale-down models** on which the design spaces and control strategy were established. The
comparability strategy compares, between the scale-down model and commercial scale: the step
yields; the CQA outcomes (glycans, charge variants, aggregate, HCP, residual DNA, leached
Protein A); and the modular viral clearance. A comparability plan describes the actions to be
taken in the event of a significant process difference at scale, including the testing program
used to demonstrate comparability between the characterized and the commercial processes
[@fda2011]. Confirmation at commercial scale is provided by the PPQ campaign and reported in
**PCMR-001**.

# Transfer of the manufacturing process

The manufacturing process is transferred by carrying the characterized set-points, normal
operating ranges (NORs) and proven acceptable ranges (PARs) into the receiving-site master
batch records, and by confirming the CPP and WC-CPP ranges at commercial scale in engineering
and PPQ batches. Of the `{python} n_params` process parameters characterized across the train,
`{python} n_cpp` are critical (`{python} n_true_cpp` CPP and `{python} n_wc` WC-CPP), and are
the parameters whose commercial-scale control the transfer must confirm; the remaining
`{python} f"{cc.get('KPP',0)}"` KPP and `{python} f"{cc.get('GPP',0)}"` GPP are transferred as
process-performance and general controls. The critical parameters and their NORs are summarized
in @tbl-cpp.

# Transfer of analytical methods

The validated release, in-process and characterization methods are transferred to the receiving-
site QC laboratory under method-transfer protocols with cross-site precision and accuracy
acceptance criteria, and co-validated before the PPQ campaign. The methods include the glycan
map, size-variant (SEC), charge-variant (icIEF), HCP, residual-DNA, leached-Protein-A and the
XMuLV/MVM infectivity assays that measure the CQAs across the train. Method equivalence between
sites is a prerequisite for the comparability and PPQ assessments; any method gap is captured in
§11.

# Transfer of the control strategy

The per-CQA control strategy defined during characterization — input-material controls,
procedural controls, process-parameter controls (CPP/WC-CPP NORs), in-process controls, and
release and characterization testing — is transferred by mapping every control element into the
receiving-site master batch records and in-process-control plan, and confirmed in PPQ. The
control strategy assures the `{python} n_cqa` CQAs at commercial scale, with the tightest
capability at the cumulative viral-clearance CQA (Cpk = `{python} f"{min_cpk:.2f}"`); the
one true CPP of the process (the low-pH viral-inactivation pH) and the
`{python} n_wc` WC-CPPs receive enhanced control. The overall control strategy is consolidated
in **PCMR-001**.

# PPQ and batch strategy

Commercial-scale confirmation is provided by a Stage-2 process performance qualification (PPQ)
campaign at the receiving site. The PPQ batches reproduce the manufacturing process, components
and composition at commercial scale and confirm the CPP ranges, the multivariate design spaces
and the cumulative viral clearance [@fda2011]. The number of PPQ batches is set by the
receiving-site validation plan (the characterization capability model uses
`{python} n_ppq` qualification batches at NOR-distributed set-points as the basis for the
commercial-scale capability estimate); the PPQ acceptance criteria are the CQA acceptance
criteria and the confirmed CPP ranges. PPQ results are reported in **PCMR-001**.

# Gap analysis

The gap analysis compares the sending and receiving sites and identifies the differences that
must be resolved before or during the transfer, each with an impact assessment, a mitigation and
a status (@tbl-gaps). Open gaps are resolved before the PPQ campaign; their closure is tracked in
the transfer record.

# Roles and responsibilities

| Function | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Technology Transfer / MSAT | Author and own the transfer plan; coordinate the transfer and gap closure |
| Sending site — Process Development | Provide the characterized process knowledge, ranges and scale-down-model data |
| Receiving site — Manufacturing | Execute engineering and PPQ batches; implement the master batch records |
| Analytical Development / QC | Transfer and co-validate the analytical methods; support comparability |
| Quality Assurance (both sites) | Approve the plan; confirm the risk assessments and control strategy; release PPQ |

: Roles and responsibilities for the transfer. {#tbl-roles}

# Schedule

The transfer proceeds in sequence: (1) site-equivalency analysis and facility/equipment
qualification; (2) analytical-method transfer and co-validation; (3) engineering runs confirming
the CPP ranges and scale-down-model comparability; (4) the Stage-2 PPQ campaign; and (5) the
Process Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**) confirming the transfer and commercial-
scale control strategy. Gap closure (§11) gates entry into the PPQ campaign.

# Risks and assumptions

The plan assumes the receiving-site facility, utilities and equipment are qualified for A-Mab
manufacture and that the analytical methods transfer with acceptable cross-site equivalence. The
principal risk is that scale effects shift a CPP range, a design space or the cumulative viral
clearance at commercial scale; this is mitigated by the scale-down-model bridge, the
site-equivalency analysis, the engineering runs and the PPQ confirmation, with the gap analysis
(§11) tracking every non-equivalence to closure before PPQ.
